'''Maria Elena Zavala''' (born 1950) is an American [[plant biologist]].<ref name=":5">{{Cite book|last=St. John, Jetty.|title=Hispanic scientists : Ellen Ochoa, Carlos A. Ramírez, Eloy Rodriguez, Lydia Villa-Komaroff, Maria Elena Zavala|date=1996|publisher=Capstone Press|isbn=1-56065-360-4|location=Mankato, MN|oclc=33861893}}</ref> She was the first Mexican-American woman to earn a PhD in botany in the United States.<ref name=":9">{{Cite web|title=Maria Elena Zavala, Ph.D., Northridge {{!}} CSU|url=https://www2.calstate.edu:443/csu-system/faculty-staff/employee-profile/2017-employee-profile/Student-Success/Pages/Maria-Elena-Zavala-PhD-Northridge.aspx|access-date=2020-09-17|website=www2.calstate.edu|language=en-US}}</ref> She is currently a full professor of biology at the [[California State University, Northridge|California State University-Northridge]], studying plant development.<ref name=":6">{{Cite web|title=Maria Elena Zavala, PhD|url=https://www.sacnas.org/team/maria-elena-zavala-phd/|access-date=2020-09-17|website=SACNAS|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":7">{{Cite web|title=MariaElena Zavala, Ph.D. {{!}} HuffPost|url=https://www.huffpost.com/author/mariaelena-zavala-phd|access-date=2020-09-17|website=www.huffpost.com|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Maria Elena Zavala {{!}} CSUN|url=https://www.csun.edu/science-mathematics/biology/maria-elena-zavala|access-date=2020-09-17|website=CSUN College of Science and Math|date=29 October 2013 }}</ref> She is a Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]], the first Latina fellow of the [[American Society of Plant Biologists]], the first Latina fellow of the [[American Society for Cell Biology|American Society of Cell Biology]], and an elected fellow of the Institute of Science.<ref name=":7" /><ref name=":9"/><ref name=":10">{{Cite web|last=Hale|first=Danielle|title=CSUN receives grant to help minority students in biomedical field|url=https://sundial.csun.edu/55632/news/csun-receives-grant-to-help-minority-students-in-biomedical-field/|access-date=2020-09-17|website=The Sundial}}</ref><ref name=":12">{{Cite web|date=2017-11-02|title=American Society of Cell Biology Names CSUN Professor First Latina Fellow|url=https://scvnews.com/american-society-of-cell-biology-names-csun-professor-first-latina-fellow/|access-date=2020-09-17|website=SCVNews.com|language=en-US}}</ref> In 2000, she was awarded the [[Presidential Award for Excellence in Science, Mathematics, and Engineering Mentoring]], which recognizes individuals who have increased the participation of underrepresented minorities in their fields.<ref name=":7" /><ref name=":11">{{Cite web|title=PAESMEM » Awardee Profile|url=https://paesmem.net/paesmemRecognition/awardeeProfile/1059|access-date=2020-09-17|website=paesmem.net}}</ref><ref name=":13">{{Cite web|last=Garcia|first=Irene|date=2000-09-08|title=CSUN Professor Hailed as Model for Minorities|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2000-sep-08-me-17519-story.html|access-date=2020-09-17|website=Los Angeles Times|language=en-US}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Zavala grew up in [[La Verne, California]], and was one of five children.<ref name=":6" /><ref name=":5" /> When she was young, her parents were farm workers and picked lemons in the farms of Southern California.<ref name=":6" />

She credits her interest in plant biology to her grandmother, who was a [[Curandero|curandera]] (a traditional medicine healer), and her father, who grew roses in their garden.<ref name=":6" /> She carried out her first experiments in plant biology at the age of seven, when she compared the growth of lentils in the sunlight and in the shade.<ref name=":5" />

In high school, she worked as a teaching assistant in chemistry and biology.<ref name=":6" /> She was also in her school band.<ref name=":6" />

Zavala went to [[Pomona College]], where she majored in botany in 1972.<ref name=":6" /><ref name=":7" /><ref name=":5" /> She was awarded a [[Ford Foundation]] doctoral fellowship to continue her studies, and went on to do a PhD in plant cell biology alongside William Jensen and botanist Robert Ornduff at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], graduating in 1978.<ref name=":6" /><ref name=":7" /><ref name=":13" /> <ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=September–October 1994 |title=ASPP Newsletter |url=https://aspb.org/newsletter/archive/1994/1994SeptOct.pdf |access-date=10 Oct 2026 |website=ASPP Newsletter}}</ref> She is also the first Chicana to graduate from UC Berkeley's botany department.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-10-28 |title=Insight Fall 2020 {{!}} Alumni Profile - Maria Elena Zavala |url=https://ib.berkeley.edu/newsletter/fall-2020/alumni-profile |access-date=2026-02-23 |website=Integrative Biology |language=en}}</ref>  Zavala is credited to be the first Mexican American in the United States to graduate with a PhD in botany.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Notable CSUN Women in STEM {{!}} CSUN University Library |url=https://library.csun.edu/wise/notable-women-in-stem |access-date=2025-09-11 |website=library.csun.edu}}</ref>

== Research and career ==
After completing her PhD she went on to work as a postdoctoral associate at Indiana University, as a staff researcher for the [[United States Department of Agriculture]], [[Yale University]] as a postdoctoral fellow, and well as [[Michigan State University]] as a visiting professor.<ref name=":7" /><ref name=":1" />She has worked at the [[California State University, Northridge|California State University-Northridge]] since 1988.<ref name=":11" /> In May of 1994 she was awarded Outstanding Professor to an American Society of Plant Physiologist member. Zavala was very busy during this time teaching two undergraduate courses, one graduate course, leading an active research program and being an adviser to master's degree candidates. <ref name=":1" />

Zavala's research focuses on plant development, specifically the structure of roots.<ref name=":7" /><ref name=":5" /> "As a researcher, she uses plants as model systems to investigate problems in development and growth."<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-10-28 |title=Insight Fall 2020 {{!}} Alumni Profile - Maria Elena Zavala |url=https://ib.berkeley.edu/newsletter/fall-2020/alumni-profile |access-date=2026-10-03 |website=Integrative Biology |language=en}}</ref> She focuses her research on beans and corn, with the aim of creating crops that can resist cooler temperatures.<ref name=":5" /> Her research has been funded by the [[National Science Foundation]], the United States Department of Agriculture, and the [[National Institutes of Health]].<ref name=":7" /><ref>{{Cite web|date=2013-08-14|title=NIH Continues MariaElena Zavala Partnership|url=https://csunshinetoday.csun.edu/faculty-and-staff-news/nih-continues-mariaelena-zavala-partnership/}}</ref>

Zavala has also taken a keen interest in education equity, by helping to develop science curricula, and by establishing and directing programs to champion the participation of women and minorities in science.<ref name=":7" /> For example, she has been involved in American Women in Science, Women in Science and Engineering, [[Women in Cell Biology (WICB)|Women in Cell Biology]], the American Society of Plant Biologists Minority Affairs Committee, and the American Society for Cell Biology Minority Affairs Committee.<ref name=":7" /> Between 2001 and 2002, Zavala also served as the first [[Chicano|Chicana]] president of the [[Society for the Advancement of Chicanos/Hispanics and Native Americans in Science|Society of Advancement of Chicanos and Native Americans in Science]].<ref name=":7" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=Board of Directors|url=https://www.sacnas.org/who-we-are/board-staff-commitees/board-of-directors/|access-date=2020-09-17|website=SACNAS|language=en-US}}</ref> She spoke at the 2017 Los Angeles March for Science.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Salinas|first=Lorena|title=CSUN biology professor to address issues concerning the underprivileged at L.A. March for Science|url=https://sundial.csun.edu/111053/news/csun-biology-professor-the-underprivileged-at-l-a-march-for-science/|access-date=2020-09-17|website=The Sundial}}</ref> In 2019, Zavala co-authored a paper advocating for minorities in her field, titled "Improving Underrepresented Minority Student Persistence in STEM."<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Estrada |first=Mica |last2=Burnett |first2=Myra |last3=Campbell |first3=Andrew G. |last4=Campbell |first4=Patricia B. |last5=Denetclaw |first5=Wilfred F. |last6=Gutiérrez |first6=Carlos G. |last7=Hurtado |first7=Sylvia |last8=John |first8=Gilbert H. |last9=Matsui |first9=John |last10=McGee |first10=Richard |last11=Okpodu |first11=Camellia Moses |last12=Robinson |first12=T. Joan |last13=Summers |first13=Michael F. |last14=Werner-Washburne |first14=Maggie |last15=Zavala |first15=MariaElena |date=September 2016 |title=Improving Underrepresented Minority Student Persistence in STEM |url=https://www.lifescied.org/doi/10.1187/cbe.16-01-0038 |journal=CBE: Life Sciences Education |volume=15 |issue=3 |pages=es5 |doi=10.1187/cbe.16-01-0038 |pmc=5008901 |pmid=27543633}}</ref> In 2022, Zavala was named a Fellow of the California Academy of Sciences. <ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-03-10 |title=CSUN Biology Professor MariaElena Zavala Named a California Academy of Sciences Fellow |url=https://csunshinetoday.csun.edu/university-news/csun-biology-professor-mariaelena-zavala-named-a-california-academy-of-sciences-fellow/ |access-date=2025-03-06 |website=CSUN Today |language=en-US}}</ref> 

Additionally, she has been the director of CSUN’s Maximizing Access to Research Careers (MARC) Undergraduate Student Training in Academic Research (U-STAR) program since 1990, as well as the Research Initiatives for Scientific Enhancement (RISE) since 1993.<ref name=":9" /><ref>{{Cite web|date=2014-06-12|title=Maria Elena Zavala Continues 'MARC USTAR' Project|url=https://csunshinetoday.csun.edu/faculty-and-staff-news/maria-elena-zavala-continues-marc-ustar-project/|access-date=2020-09-17|website=CSUN Today}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2017-04-25|title=CSUN biology professor to speak at March for Science Los Angeles|url=https://busecon.csun.edu/build-poder/news/csun-biology-professor-speak-march-science-los-angeles|access-date=2020-09-17|website=CSUN}}</ref><ref name=":10" /><ref>{{Cite report |last=Zavala|first=Mariaelena |title=MARC U-STAR At California State University, Northridge |url=https://grantome.com/grant/NIH/T34-GM008395-24 |language=en}}</ref>{{Excessive citations inline|date=September 2020}}

Zavala contributed to the book "Flor y Ciencia: Chicanas in Mathematics, Science and Engineering."<ref name=":7" /><ref>{{Cite book |title=Flor y ciencia : Chicanas in science, mathematics, and engineering |date=2006 |publisher=The Adelante Project |author=Cantú, Norma E. |isbn=0-9786820-0-9 |location=San Antonio, Tex. |oclc=71083883}}</ref> 

== Awards and honours ==
Zavala is a Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].<ref name=":7" /> In 2000, she became the first woman to become president of [[SACNAS]], the Society for the Advancement of Chicanos and Native Americans in Science,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Adam |first1=Michelle |date=December 17, 2001 |title=Setting an Example for Students Nationwide: Maria Elena Zavala, First Latina President of SACNAS |journal=The Hispanic Outlook in Higher Education |volume=12 |issue=6 |pages=17 }}</ref> and in 2016 she became the first Latina fellow of the [[American Society of Plant Biologists]].<ref name=":7" /><ref name=":9"/><ref>{{Cite web|last=Garcia|first=Agustin|title=Biology professor Maria Elena Zavala shares historic research on plant cells|url=https://sundial.csun.edu/113934/news/biology-professor-maria-elena-zavala-shares-historic-research-on-plant-cells/|access-date=2020-09-17|website=The Sundial}}</ref> The next year, she became the first Latina fellow of the [[American Society for Cell Biology]].<ref name=":12" /> [[Bill Clinton|William Jefferson Clinton]] awarded her the [[Presidential Award for Excellence in Science, Mathematics, and Engineering Mentoring]] in 2000.<ref name=":7" /><ref name=":11" />  In 2020 Zavala was named one of the 100 most inspiring Latinx/Hispanic scientists in the United States by [[Cell Press]] journal.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://csunshinetoday.csun.edu/science-and-technology/zavala-named-one-of-the-most-inspiring-hispaniclatinx-scientists-in-america/ |title=Zavala Named One of the Most Inspiring Hispanic/Latinx Scientists in America |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=November 5, 2020 |website=CSUN Today |publisher=[[California State University, Northridge]] |access-date=November 24, 2020 }}</ref> In 2024, Zavala helped get about $490,000 in funding to support a program that helps minority students prepare for careers in biomedical research<ref>{{Cite web |last=Chandler |first=Carmen Ramos |date=2021-01-20 |title=CSUN Receives $2M to Help Graduate Students ‘Bridge’ to a Ph.D. - CSUN Newsroom |url=https://newsroom.csun.edu/2021/01/20/csun-receives-2m-to-help-graduate-students-bridge-to-a-ph-d/ |access-date=2026-02-17 |language=en-US}}</ref>
